European Parliament votes to refer matter to EU Court of Justice, thereby freezing ratification process for agreement | AGENCE EUROPE

# European Parliament votes to refer matter to EU Court of Justice, thereby freezing ratification process for agreement

 Brussels, 21/01/2026 (Agence Europe) 

On Wednesday 21 January, in a very close vote that came down to 10 votes (334 votes in favour, 324 against, 9 abstentions), the European Parliament adopted a referral to the Court of Justice of the European Union (CJEU) to assess the compatibility of the EU/Mercosur agreement - signed in Paraguay on 17 January - with the EU Treaties.

The effect of this vote is to freeze Parliament’s ratification process until the Court issues its judgment, which could take more than a year.

A spokesperson for the European Commission said he strongly regretted the outcome of the vote “ at a time when EU producers and exporters urgently need access to new markets”. He also felt that the institution had already responded to Parliament’s concerns in the past.

According to the Commission, the agreement “ will not reduce audit and control measures for agricultural imports from Mercosur” and “ will not compromise the EU’s strict sanitary and phytosanitary standards, the precautionary principle and the safety of European consumers”.

A majority of MEPs, who supported the request to refer the matter to the Court of Justice of the European Union, are not convinced and also question the splitting of the agreement into two parts and the rebalancing mechanism (see EUROPE 13790/22).

“ The Court will have to assess the extent to which the rebalancing mechanism allowing Mercosur countries to challenge European legislation that they consider harmful to their exports is compatible with European law and the EU’s regulatory autonomy”, explained Saskia Bricmont (Greens/EFA, Belgian).

While the fault lines over the Mercosur agreement are more national (see EUROPE 13790/22), the Chair of the Committee on International Trade, Germany’s Bernd Lange (S&D), described the outcome of the vote as “ irresponsible” and “ very damaging for our economic interests and our status”.

Provisional application. However, several sources indicate that some MEPs from different political groups supporting the EU/Mercosur agreement still voted in favour of referring the matter to the Court, in the belief that provisional application of the agreement would take place anyway.

As we have mentioned on several occasions, it is indeed technically possible for the European Commission to apply the agreement provisionally with one (or more) Mercosur countries that have finalised their ratification process - regardless of Parliament’s final consent vote.

However, this decision could tarnish the trust between the two institutions. Many MEPs have warned against this possibility.

Opinions differ: Wednesday’s vote on the opinion of the CJEU would make the European Commission more cautious about the idea of triggering this provisional application. On the contrary, its decision could now be precipitated, given that the parliamentary ratification process is blocked. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz explicitly called on Wednesday for the agreement to be applied provisionally.

For the time being, the Commission has indicated that it will “ enter into dialogue with the EU Council and MEPs before deciding on the next steps”. The issue may be discussed at the extraordinary European summit on Thursday evening.

For details of the vote and the resolution: https://aeur.eu/f/kc4 ; https://aeur.eu/f/kc3 (Original version in French by Pauline Denys)
